content: RSS never had a big corporation acting as a benefactor, but to some extent Harvard did play that role, though it didn't have an ego when it came to this stuff, and it didn't behave like a tech corporation (good thing!), but it was at Harvard that the podcasting bootstrap centered. Is that why imho RSS hasn't been considered as the backbone of the social web? Probably more than the Fog Of War nature of tech development. We have so many forks of so many things we don't know what anyone else is doing. It's easier to invent your own than figure out what the other thing did. Perhaps ChatGPT et al will change that. Yesterday I used it to get an understanding of how the content:encoded element came to exist and evolved, and you'd think I of all people would know, but I didn't. ChatGPT did. We also used to have tech journalism that covered this stuff, but that ended with BYTE and Dr Dobbs. Maybe we can restart that in some systematic way. Again we don't have communication, so we make unnecessarily slow progress as a result.
